text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with two changed-quantity, two reordered and two moved-negation quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023 reporting year, the Kessaru Health Alliance distributed 48,200 long-lasting insecticidal nets across four districts of Lower Mbenda Province. Household coverage reached 87 percent, exceeding the target agreed with the Thornfield Foundation by six points. Community volunteers assisted clinic nurses with hang-up visits in 1,140 villages, and confirmed malaria cases at partner clinics fell from 3,900 to 2,650 between January and December. However, the campaign reached the lakeshore villages but not the island settlements of Lake Pema, where flooding closed boat routes for nine weeks. Net retention surveys found that older nets were often repurposed for fishing rather than discarded. We have not yet secured funding for the 2024 replacement cycle, and we ask the Foundation to consider a bridging grant.

variants.changed_quantity_2: the lakeshore villages but not the island settlements of Lake Pema, where flooding closed boat routes for five weeks.

variants.moved_negation: We have yet secured funding for the 2024 replacement cycle, and we ask the Foundation not to consider a bridging grant.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Sabelo Dryland Seeds Project, covering March 2022 to August 2023, finds steady but uneven progress. Of the 2,400 smallholder households enrolled, 1,730 planted at least one drought-tolerant sorghum or cowpea variety in the last season, a 72 percent adoption rate. Yields on demonstration plots averaged 1.4 tonnes per hectare, compared with 0.9 tonnes on control plots. In most villages, women adopted the new varieties faster than men, but men still controlled most seed sales. Farmer field schools ran in Wereda West but not in Wereda East, where the extension officer post remained vacant for seven months. The evaluators recommend expanding seed fairs rather than irrigation pilots, which have not shown cost-effective results so far.

passages.source_passage: In the highland municipality of San Ilario de las Cumbres, only 41 percent of girls who complete sixth grade enrol in lower secondary school, compared with 63 percent of boys. Since 2019, Fundación Puente Claro has awarded 315 scholarships covering fees, uniforms and transport to the regional institute in Villa Morena. Retention among scholars has been strong: 88 percent remained enrolled after two years. Yet many families told our field staff that during harvest months girls are expected not to study but to care for younger siblings. According to our 2022 household survey, mothers more often than fathers support continued schooling for daughters. Scholars from the three most remote villages travel not by bus but on foot, often for ninety minutes each way.

passages.source_passage: At the midpoint of the Little Steps Playgroup Network in Orrin Valley, 26 playgroups are running against a target of 30. Between September 2022 and June 2023, 540 children aged two to five attended at least ten sessions, and caregiver attendance averaged 68 percent. Developmental screening showed language scores improving faster than motor scores. Facilitators were trained not by the network itself but by the district health office, which has created gaps in follow-up coaching. Several sites lack shaded outdoor space, and two playgroups opened in the dry season but not in the rainy season, when their venues flooded. On average, grandmothers attended more regularly than fathers, a pattern the evaluators had not anticipated.

passages.source_passage: Since its launch in April 2021, the Hollin Bridge Family Reunification Service has registered 212 separated or unaccompanied children in the Tavari border districts. Most referrals came from border police rather than from schools. By the mid-term point, caseworkers had traced relatives for 147 children, and 96 have been reunified after a home assessment. Tracing took longer for adolescents than for younger children. Foster carers said they valued not the cash stipend but the monthly visits from caseworkers. The evaluation found that most reunified children received follow-up visits in the first month but not after the third month, as the protocol requires. Eleven children remain in emergency foster placements beyond the 90-day limit, and four of the nine caseworkers left during 2023.

passages.source_passage: Residents of the Quenmoor river settlements live, on average, 64 kilometres from the nearest magistrate's court, and the district has only three practising lawyers for roughly 180,000 people. Since 2020, the Open Gate Justice Centre has trained 38 community paralegals who hold weekly clinics in market towns. In 2023 they handled 1,912 cases, most involving land boundaries, inheritance and unpaid wages. Land disputes take far longer to resolve than wage claims. Paralegals may advise clients but not represent them in court, so complex cases go to the Centre's two staff lawyers. Clients told us they trusted paralegals more than local chiefs. With current funding, we will be able to sustain the existing clinics but not extend them to the northern settlements.

passages.source_passage: Youth unemployment in Marrowgate County stands at 34 percent, and more than half of young people who leave school before age sixteen have never held a formal job. The Brightforge Vocational Centre opened in 2018 and has since graduated 1,260 trainees in welding, solar installation, tailoring and motorcycle repair. A 2023 tracer study found that 61 percent of graduates were employed or self-employed six months after completion. Most graduates found work in towns rather than in their home villages. Employers preferred practical experience over formal certificates, yet our courses currently include only two weeks of workplace placement. Female trainees enrolled mostly in tailoring but not in solar installation, where wages are highest. This proposal seeks support to lengthen placements to eight weeks and recruit twenty employer partners.

passages.source_passage: The Ashwell Basin Cash for Food Programme began monthly transfers of 45 dollars to 3,600 households in October 2022. At mid-term, the share of households reporting fewer than two meals a day had fallen from 39 percent to 17 percent. Most recipients spent transfers first on staple grains and then on school costs. Payments were made through mobile money rather than at distribution points, which reduced travel time but excluded some elderly recipients without phones. Eighteen months in, transfer values have been adjusted for household size but not for inflation, even though maize prices rose by roughly a third. Market traders did not raise prices in response to the programme, according to monthly price monitoring.

passages.source_passage: This monitoring report covers the Pelluna Coast Early Warning Programme from January to June 2024. Siren towers are now installed in 22 of 25 target fishing villages, and 410 volunteers have completed first-response training. During the cyclone alert of 14 March, SMS warnings reached 92 percent of registered phones within thirty minutes. However, the alert reached village committees before the district radio station, which delayed public broadcasts by over an hour. Fishers said they trusted the sirens more than the text messages. Evacuation drills were held in the dry months but not in the monsoon season, when risk is highest. Three siren towers did not function during testing because their solar batteries had corroded.

passages.source_passage: In the Kambaro district of northern Seyenne, a 2023 survey of 1,800 pupils found that 37 percent arrive at school without having eaten breakfast. Teachers report that hungry children concentrate poorly after mid-morning, and absenteeism peaks during the lean season from June to August. The Sahel Bowl Initiative has served daily hot meals in 14 primary schools since 2021, sourcing millet and cowpeas from local women's cooperatives. Over two years, enrolment rose by 12 percent in participating schools but not in neighbouring schools. Attendance gains have been larger for girls than for boys. Parents told us they value the hot meals more than the take-home rations. The current kitchens are equipped with firewood hearths but not with fuel-efficient stoves.
